Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tidymontage (development version)

  • Grid rows and columns can differ in shape: panels in a row share a height and panels in a column a width, instead of all panels sharing one shape. For example, a row of square crops can sit above a row of flat zoom strips (y = view), or images of another shape can fill a row of their own. Shapes that don’t line up still give an error, now naming a panel.

  • layout_hero(stack = TRUE) stacks the side panels so that each is as long as the hero’s edge: strips below the hero as wide as the hero, or beside it as high as the hero. Side panels can have another shape than the hero, for example a flat zoom of each channel under a big merge.

  • Rotated crops and zooms: add_crop() and add_zoom() take an angle, in degrees counterclockwise as Fiji measures lines, or an angle column in center for an angle per image. Rotated regions are shown upright and sampled with bilinear interpolation. Zooms take the angle of the crop unless given one. Zoom boxes, arrowheads and preview_positions() follow the rotation. get_panels() has a new angle column.

  • Several zooms per image: call add_zoom() again for each. With two or more, zooms are numbered in the order they were added: the number is shown in the top-left corner of each box and each zoom panel, and the views are named "zoom 1", "zoom 2", … A new label argument sets your own label or turns it off. preview_positions() outlines all zooms.

  • New tidymontage_options() sets session-wide defaults for the size box, its units and the gap, like tidyplots_options().

  • New add_arrows() marks locations with arrowheads. They belong to an image and are drawn in all of its panels: each channel, merges, overlays, crops and zooms.

  • New lut() colours channels and overlays with a colormap such as magma or viridis, in adjust_colors() and add_overlay(color = ). In merges, such channels use their original colour. add_color_legend() shows them as colour bars labelled with the display range (ranges = TRUE).

  • Initial CRAN submission.

Developed by Jan Broder Engler.
